key_insight: Bayesian inference applied to photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize whether perovskite solar-cell degradation originates at the electron-transport layer, hole-transport layer, or within the bulk.
engineering_relevance: This gives device engineers a practical diagnostic tool to target the specific interfaces causing stability loss and to evaluate passivation strategies more effectively.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to measured optoelectronic behavior
Bayesian inference to generate spatial parameter maps and track them during aging
evidence_signal: The authors aged devices at 70 °C under full-spectrum sunlight and observed time-evolving, spatially non-uniform parameter maps that identified pronounced degradation at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The inferred maps depend on model assumptions and image-to-parameter identifiability, so results should be validated against independent physical measurements.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
